props.gloss_en: an animal giving birth to a firstborn with difficulty -- he cuts [the fetus] limb by limb and casts it to the dogs
if its majority emerged -- it must be buried, and [the mother] is exempt from the firstborn [law thereafter]
a third emerged and he sold it to a gentile, then another third emerged -- Rav Huna: it is holy
Rabba: it is not holy
a third emerged through the wall and two thirds through the womb -- Rav Huna: it is not holy
Rabba: it is holy
[Rav Huna] holds: [the firstborn] is holy retroactively
[Rabba] holds: [the firstborn] is holy from here on
once its majority emerged it is revealed retroactively that it was holy from the start, and what he sold -- he sold nothing
and what he sold -- he sold properly
and the first majority was not in [i.e. did not emerge through] the womb
and a majority came out through the womb

had we been taught only this [the gentile case], [one would say] Rav Huna said it here because it is lenient, but in that [the wall case], which is stringent, say he concedes to Rabba -- so the wall dispute was needed
and had it been stated only in that [the wall case], [one would say] Rabba said it there, but in this one say he concedes to Rav Huna -- it is necessary
no -- here we deal with one who cuts and casts [each limb away]
that is indeed what it says: when is this said -- when he cuts and casts; but if he cuts and leaves [the limbs] -- it is as though its majority emerged, and it must be buried
rival framing: [the dilemma is] where the majority [of the fetus] emerged with a minority of a limb
survivor framing: where half [the fetus] emerged with the majority of a limb, and he asks: the minority [of that limb] inside -- is it cast after the limb's majority?
it is obvious that we do not leave the majority of the fetus and go after the majority of a limb
the entertained resolution: [the mishna's 'its majority'] is where half emerged with the majority of a limb -- so the inner minority of the limb is cast after the limb's majority
no -- [the mishna is] where its majority emerged with a minority of a limb, and it teaches that we do not leave the majority of the animal's fetus and go after the limb
in its own afterbirth? that is its [normal] way!
rival framing: if it came out head-first -- it has [already] exempted [the womb]!
survivor framing: where it came out feet-first
it brought it out? then [the weasel] took it out!
uprooted? then they are not there!
the walls of the womb were thinned -- what is the law?
R' Zeira: you have touched on a dilemma that was raised by us
he was in doubt only where the breached part exceeds the standing part, since there is some standing part; but [walls] thinned -- he was in no doubt

questions.gloss_en: Rava: does one follow the majority with limbs, or not? (framed at 70a.9 as half the fetus out with the majority of a limb; the resolution attempted at 70a.10-11 is deflected and no verdict is recorded)
Rava: he wrapped it in palm bast -- what is the law?
Rava: in his robe -- what is the law?
Rava, as reformulated by the stam: in another [animal's] afterbirth -- what is the law?
Rava: [a hand] wrapped it, held it and brought it out -- what is the law? (framed by the stam as feet-first)
Rava, as reformulated by the stam: a weasel swallowed it and took it out, brought it back in and vomited it, and it came out by itself -- what is the law?
Rava: he pressed two wombs together, and it left this one and entered that one -- does [a womb's] own [fetus] alone exempt, or another's too? teiku
Rav Acha: the walls of the womb opened wide -- does the womb's airspace sanctify, which is present, or contact with the womb, which is absent? (no verdict recorded)
Mar bar Rav Ashi, as reformulated by the stam: the walls were uprooted and hung on its neck -- do they sanctify only in their place, or out of place too? (no verdict recorded)

R' Zeira (or, some say, R' Zeira of R' Asi): the standing part exceeds the breach and it came out through the breach; the breach exceeds the standing part and it came out through the standing part -- what is the law? (no verdict recorded)
